title: Playbook Creator Playbook
description: Meta-playbook for creating domain-specific playbooks. Produces structured JSON playbooks through 16 phases of research, KB construction and bootstrapping, architecture, task engineering, assembly, validation, and structured dry-run. Works with single-agent systems where one agent fills multiple functional roles; output playbooks may optionally use role-based-multi-agent with per-role agent_assignment.
phase_summary: Phase 0: Commission & Scoping — Define purpose, scope, constraints, complexity profile. Agent must acknowledge all 16 phases.
Phase 1: Domain Research — Research domain, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive landscape.
Phase 2: KB Architecture — Design knowledge base layers, schemas, bridge mappings, population strategy.
Phase 3: KB Bootstrapping — Create directory tree, seed entries, harvest research content, validate schema conformance.
Phase 4: Process Architecture — Design output playbook phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, gates.
Phase 5: Role Engineering — Define functional roles for the output playbook: who does what, who approves, decision authority.
Phase 6: Task Engineering — Write detailed task descriptions, execution guides, and templates for each phase.
Phase 7: Output Configuration — Define workflow model, roles, usage instructions, compilation tuning, KB mapping.
Phase 8: Metrics & KPI Definition — Define process, quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets.
Phase 9: JSON Assembly — Assemble complete output playbook JSON from all design documents.
Phase 10: JSON Validation & Consistency — Validate assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review.
Phase 11: Quality Audit — Gap Analysis — Systematic audit against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, and completeness.
Phase 12: Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run — Walk through the playbook under structured scenarios to find issues.
Phase 13: Stakeholder Review & Iteration — Final human review before pilot testing.
Phase 14: Documentation & Version Control — Package the final playbook with supporting documentation.
Phase 15: Continuous Improvement — After each run of the output playbook, review and optionally improve it.

Coordinator.description: Phase gates, tracking, status updates, blocker escalation, decisions ledger and artifact manifest maintenance
Coordinator.role_context: Track progress systematically. Verify conditions before advancing. Maintain decisions-ledger and artifact-manifest at every gate.

Researcher.description: Domain research, best practices, SME knowledge, competitive analysis
Researcher.role_context: Gather broadly, synthesize precisely. Cite sources. Distinguish facts from opinions. Flag gaps in knowledge.

Architect.description: Phase structure, task granularity, role design, dependency mapping, template design
Architect.role_context: Design for clarity and separation. Every boundary must be justified. Every dependency must be explicit. Favor simplicity.

Builder.description: Task titles/descriptions, JSON assembly, validation, implementation of fixes
Builder.role_context: Mechanical precision. Follow specifications exactly. Verify output matches input requirements. No creative interpretation during assembly.

Auditor.description: Quality review, scenario walkthroughs, gap analysis, stress testing, failure mode cataloging, contamination testing, final verification before handoff
Auditor.role_context: Binary yes/no judgments, no hedging. Find what is broken. Review with fresh eyes. Do not defend previous work.

Stakeholder.description: Purpose, scope, constraints, success criteria, business decisions, final approval
Stakeholder.role_context: Business alignment. Does this serve the commission? Are constraints respected? Would you trust this playbook to run unsupervised?

in_scope: Knowledge base bootstrapping (directory creation, placeholder seeding, initial harvesting)
Structured dry-run validation with scenario matrix
out_of_scope: Executing the produced playbook (that is the user's responsibility)
Full KB curation and ongoing maintenance (the creator bootstraps the KB with placeholders and initial harvesting; full curation is the user's responsibility)
Multi-agent orchestration of the creation process itself (the creator runs as single-agent; output playbooks may use role-based-multi-agent with per-role agent_assignment)
adjacent: Skills/prompting frameworks that may be activated per-phase
Knowledge bases built from the produced KB specification
CI/CD or version control for produced playbooks

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Quality Standard
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Every produced playbook must be comprehensive enough that any team can execute it without ambiguity. Every task must have an owner. Every non-obvious task must have a description. Every phase must have a gate with explicit conditions. No placeholder content.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Embed as a verification checklist item in task descriptions where this concern applies. The item must be a concrete yes/no check, not a restatement of the concern.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Role Consistency
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Roles defined at playbook start must be used consistently throughout all tasks. Every task title must start with [Role]. Roles cannot appear fewer than 3 times (orphaned) or reference undefined roles.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Include role consistency verification as an explicit gate condition at phases where tasks are written or assembled.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Gate Enforcement
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Phase gates are firewall points — nothing advances until all conditions are met. Each gate must list explicit conditions, blocker examples, and handoff blocks. Conditions must be verifiable, not subjective.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Include gate completeness as a pre_check condition in compilation blocks for phases that define or validate gates.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Deliverable Tracking
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Every task that produces output must name the file path. The artifact manifest and metrics tracker are persistent files that must be updated at every phase gate. Later phases reference earlier deliverables through handoff chains.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every task that produces a deliverable must have an 'output' field with the exact file path. At every phase gate: (1) artifact-manifest.md must be updated to reflect all files produced in that phase, (2) metrics-tracker.md must be updated with any measurable metrics from that phase. Stale persistent files (not updated since a prior phase) are a gate failure.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Context Preservation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, and metrics-tracker.md are persistent tracking files. decisions-ledger and artifact-manifest are loaded in every phase and updated at every gate. No decision rationale is silently lost across session boundaries.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Verify decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md appear in every phase's context_load (except Phase 0). Verify both are updated at every gate.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Gate Verification
cross_cutting_concerns.description: At every phase gate, the executing agent must produce a GATE VERIFICATION block listing each condition with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). No condition may be marked PASS without evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every gate task description must require the agent to output the verification block format. Gates without explicit PASS/FAIL evidence are treated as not checked.

cross_cutting_concerns.title: Path Configuration Compliance
cross_cutting_concerns.description: All file operations use configured paths from Phase 0. No hardcoded external paths.
cross_cutting_concerns.enforcement_rule: Every phase that reads external files must reference paths from scope.md configuration section.

entry_schema._note: The creator itself uses no structured KB. Output playbooks define their own KB architecture in Phase 2.

population_strategy.placeholder_seeding: N/A — the creator has no KB to seed

items.title: [Coordinator] — Establish configuration
items.description:
Ask the user to establish runtime configuration before any other work begins:

1. OUTPUT LOCATION
   - Default: ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>/
   - Ask: "Save location: ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>/ — correct, or specify different path?"
   - If user specifies different path: use exact path provided
   - If directory exists: create ~/playbooks/<playbook-name>-v2/ (or next available: -v3, -v4, etc.)
   - Never merge or replace existing content in any directory

2. EXTERNAL DATA SOURCES
   - Ask item-by-item with explicit paths:
     * "Pull knowledge base from [path]? (yes/no)"
     * "Pull other playbooks from [path]? (yes/no)"
     * "Pull references from [path]? (yes/no)"
   - Record all decisions in scope.md configuration section
   - Only access sources user explicitly approved
   - If no external sources needed, document "No external data sources required"

Output: scope.md with configuration section documenting all decisions.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Create project knowledge base folder
items.description:
Folder structure: README.md, research/, architecture/, drafts/, audits/, testing/, final/

Initialize decisions-ledger.md — empty, with header: '# Decisions Ledger — append at every phase gate'

Initialize artifact-manifest.md — empty, with header: '# Artifact Manifest — update at every phase gate' and columns: File | Phase | Status | Summary

Initialize metrics-tracker.md — empty, with header: '# Metrics Tracker — record at every phase gate' and columns: Metric | Phase | Value | Target | Date
items.output: README.md, project folder structure, decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, metrics-tracker.md

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define the playbook's purpose and problem statement
items.description:
Answer precisely:
- What process does this playbook automate/guide?
- What problem does it solve? What goes wrong without it?
- Is this new, an optimization of existing, or a variant?

One paragraph, no ambiguity.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define target users and team composition
items.description:
Who will RUN this playbook?
- Team size, roles, skill levels
- What tools/access do they have?

The playbook's detail level is calibrated to the least experienced person who will use it.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define scope boundaries
items.description:
IN SCOPE: what this playbook covers
OUT OF SCOPE: what it does NOT cover
ADJACENT: what it connects to but doesn't own

Scope creep is the #1 killer of playbook quality.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define success criteria for the playbook itself
items.description:
Measurable criteria (e.g., 'an unfamiliar user can execute it without clarifying questions')
Quality bar (e.g., 'every task has an owner, description, and exit criteria')
Pilot test pass/fail criteria

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Define strategic constraints
items.description:
Technology constraints, methodology constraints, budget/resource constraints, timeline constraints, compliance/legal constraints.

These become universal rules that every phase must respect.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Identify related existing playbooks
items.description:
Playbooks covering overlapping territory, upstream/downstream dependencies, reference/inspiration sources.

If replacing an existing playbook, that playbook becomes input for Phase 1 audit.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Classify domain complexity
items.description:
Answer three questions to set complexity guardrails for the creation process:

1. PROCESS COMPLEXITY: How many distinct phases does the real-world process have?
   - Simple (1-4 phases): single-skill workflow, linear steps
   - Standard (5-10 phases): multi-skill workflow, some parallelism
   - Complex (11+ phases): multi-discipline workflow, significant dependencies

2. KNOWLEDGE COMPLEXITY: How many distinct types of knowledge does the domain require?
   - Flat (1 type): single reference layer, no translation needed
   - Layered (2-3 types): multiple knowledge domains, some cross-referencing
   - Bridged (4+ types): distinct vocabularies that need translation between them

3. ROLE COMPLEXITY: How many distinct functional roles does the process need?
   - Minimal (2 roles): one doer, one approver
   - Standard (3-4 roles): specialized functions with handoffs
   - Full (5+ roles): distinct disciplines with complex handoff chains

Record the complexity_profile in decisions-ledger.md:
  process: simple|standard|complex
  knowledge: flat|layered|bridged
  roles: minimal|standard|full
  overall: highest of the three dimensions

The overall classification sets advisory guardrails (not hard limits) for the rest of the creation process.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Read and acknowledge all phases
items.description:
Read this playbook's phase_summary field (or scan all phase titles and purposes). Produce a one-line summary per phase in decisions-ledger.md under heading '## Phase Inventory'. This ensures the executing agent knows the full 16-phase scope before starting work.

Do NOT skip this task. Execution collapse (FM-026) occurs when an agent reads only early phases and synthesizes later ones from imagination.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Plan session boundaries
items.description:
Based on the session_strategy in this playbook's usage_instructions, document planned session breaks in decisions-ledger.md. Record which phases share sessions and where fresh sessions start.

Session breaks should align with phase gates where decisions-ledger.md is updated.

Verify: every phase (0-15) appears in exactly one session group. No phase is orphaned or double-counted.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Purpose defined, scope locked, constraints documented, success criteria measurable, knowledge base initialized
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). No condition may be marked PASS without evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 1.
gate_conditions: Configuration established (output location + external data decisions documented in scope.md)
Purpose statement is one paragraph with no ambiguity
Scope has explicit in/out/adjacent lists
Success criteria are measurable, not subjective
Strategic constraints documented
Project knowledge base folder created
decisions-ledger.md, artifact-manifest.md, and metrics-tracker.md initialized
Complexity profile documented in decisions-ledger.md (process, knowledge, roles, overall)
Phase inventory: all 16 phases acknowledged in decisions-ledger.md
Session boundaries planned and documented
blocker_examples: scope.md missing configuration section — ask user for output location and external data permissions before proceeding
Purpose statement says 'improve the process' without specifying which process or what improvement looks like — too vague, rewrite
Scope has no out-of-scope list — everything is implicitly in scope, which means scope creep is guaranteed
Success criteria say 'playbook is good' — not measurable, define what 'good' means quantitatively

excluded_files: Conversation about why scope decisions were made — resolved, captured in scope.md and decisions-ledger.md

checklists.title: Phase 1: Domain Research & Process Discovery
checklists.purpose: Understand the domain deeply enough to build a playbook for it. Research produces flat documents that Phase 2 will structure.

compilation.role_mindset: Researcher — gather, synthesize, document. Breadth over depth at this stage.
compilation.objective: Produce comprehensive flat research documents covering domain processes, best practices, competitors, cross-cutting concerns, and platform specifics
success_criteria: Domain analysis covers standard processes, failure modes, and terminology
Best practices documented with sources
Cross-cutting concerns identified with justification
Requirements document synthesizes all research

items.title: [Researcher] — Research the domain this playbook serves
items.description:
Standard processes in this industry/discipline, common failure modes, regulatory/compliance requirements, standard tools and platforms, terminology glossary, KPIs professionals track.

Source requirements: research must include at least one external source beyond any existing playbook or user-provided material. Use web search, documentation sites, published standards, or authoritative references. Cite every factual claim with its source. If replacing an existing playbook, the existing playbook is input data, not a substitute for fresh domain research.

items.title: [Researcher] — Research industry best practices and standards
items.description: Published standards (ISO, industry frameworks), expert recommendations (books, courses, authoritative sources), common process frameworks, typical phase structures, common pitfalls and how experts avoid them.

items.title: [Researcher] — Competitive playbook/template audit
items.description: Existing playbooks, templates, SOPs, checklists covering similar territory. For each: what it covers, what it does well, what it misses, structure, detail level.
items.conditional: Only if comparable playbooks/templates exist for this domain

items.title: [Researcher] — Audit existing playbook(s) being replaced
items.conditional: Only if replacing an existing playbook
items.description: What the existing playbook does well (KEEP), what it does poorly (FIX), what it's missing (ADD), what contradicts current strategy (REMOVE).

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Gather process knowledge from subject matter experts
items.description:
The actual process (not documented — the real one), steps that aren't written down, common blockers and resolutions, decisions requiring judgment vs always-the-same, what they wish they'd known before their first time.

Self-service fallback: if the commissioning user IS the domain expert (no external SMEs available), conduct a structured self-interview. Ask the user the same questions you would ask an SME: what steps are undocumented, what commonly goes wrong, what requires judgment. Record their answers in the same sme-interviews.md format. The key insight must still be captured even if the source is the user rather than a third-party expert.

items.title: [Researcher] — Identify cross-cutting concerns
items.description:
Concerns that touch every phase, not just one. Technology/platform concerns affecting all phases. Compliance concerns applying to every task. Quality standards verified at every phase. Strategic constraints shaping every decision.

Cross-cutting concerns must be woven throughout the playbook, not isolated in one phase.

items.title: [Researcher] — Identify platform/environment-specific concerns
items.description: If the playbook involves a specific platform or environment: how does data/content get stored, what are the safe modification methods, what should NEVER be done (anti-patterns), what platform-specific tools exist, what deployment/migration procedures apply.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Synthesize research into requirements document
items.description: Domain requirements (what the process must accomplish), quality requirements (standards and compliance), strategic requirements (business constraints from Phase 0), platform requirements (technical constraints), cross-cutting requirements, user requirements (what the target team needs to succeed).

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Domain researched, requirements synthesized
gate_conditions: Domain analysis covers standard processes, failure modes, and terminology
Best practices documented with cited external sources (not solely derived from existing playbooks or user-provided material)
Competitive templates audited with strengths/weaknesses
Cross-cutting concerns identified with justification
Requirements document synthesizes all research
blocker_examples: Domain analysis missing key compliance requirements — research more
No SME input gathered — interview at least one expert before proceeding
Requirements document has 'TBD' sections — complete before proceeding

next_phase_context: research/domain-analysis.md (full — needed for KB layer classification)
excluded_files: SME interview transcripts — synthesized into requirements
Rejected competitive templates — audit captured what matters
best-practices.md and platform-concerns.md — key points captured in requirements.md

checklists.title: Phase 2: KB Architecture
checklists.purpose: Convert flat research into a structured, queryable knowledge specification. This phase produces a KB ARCHITECTURE (blueprint), not the KB itself. The actual KB gets built when the output playbook is executed.

compilation.role_mindset: Architect — structuring knowledge, not gathering it. Classify, separate, define schemas.
compilation.objective: Produce a KB architecture blueprint (layers, schemas, bridge, population strategy) that an agent can build from without ambiguity
pre_check: Domain analysis exists with distinct knowledge types identified
success_criteria: KB complexity decision documented with clear rationale
If multi-layer: every knowledge type assigned to exactly one layer with separation rules
Entry schema defined with all required fields and an example entry
Population strategy defined with sources, quality criteria, and curation rules
Directory tree specified with exact file naming conventions

items.title: [Architect] — Determine KB complexity level
items.description:
Decision question: 'Do users of this playbook describe goals in language that differs from implementation language?'
  YES → structured KB with bridge layer needed (e.g., audio: 'warm' → filter cutoff 0.2-0.4)
  NO → assess if domain has enough distinct knowledge types to warrant layers

Decision question: 'Does this domain have enough distinct knowledge types to justify separate layers?'
  YES → multi-layer KB (define layers)
  NO → flat reference (single folder of markdown files with table of contents)

The minimal path is genuinely minimal: single reference layer, no bridge, no cross-references, flat file list. A folder of markdown with a TOC. That is the floor.

items.title: [Architect] — Define knowledge layers
items.conditional: Only if multi-layer KB was chosen in Task 1
items.description:
For each layer: name and domain boundary (what belongs here and what doesn't), authority score (0.0-1.0), separation rule (why this can't merge with another layer), topics within the layer.

Separation principle: knowledge that changes independently lives in separate layers.

items.title: [Architect] — Define KB entry schema
items.description:
Exact JSON structure every entry must follow.

Required fields: id ({kb-name}_{topic}_{entry-name}), kb (which layer), topic, status (placeholder|harvested|curated|synced), version (semver), title, summary, description, source, concepts (array of {name, description, related[]}), code_blocks (array of {language, code, preserved} — if domain involves code), tags, related_topics, difficulty (beginner|intermediate|advanced), domain_relevance (1-10).

Additional domain-specific fields defined here.

items.title: [Architect] — Define bridge entry schema
items.conditional: Only if KB complexity decision identified a need for creative-to-technical translation
items.description:
Bridge entry required fields: category, parameters (array), intent_mappings keyed by subjective descriptor with: parameter, value_range [min, max], typical_default, confidence (0.0-1.0), source, why (human-readable rationale), anti_patterns.

Bridge is hybrid: pre-seeded with common mappings from research, auto-generated when agent encounters unmapped concepts, feedback-enriched when user evaluation refines entries.

Combination layer: bridge entries can be composed. Cross-reference individual entries, identify compatible parameter ranges, flag conflicts between anti_patterns, propose combined recipe with lower confidence score.

items.title: [Architect] — Define population strategy
items.description:
Placeholder seeding: what entries get created as placeholders during playbook setup (minimum one per topic per layer, with fallback content).
Harvesting: where content comes from, quality criteria for harvested content.
Curation rules: what must happen before harvested content becomes curated.
Sync rules: how curated entries get indexed.
Versioning protocol: entries are append-only. Existing entries are never edited — they are superseded by new entries tagged with the relevant version. Old entries remain for reference or rollback. Queries filter by version tag.

items.title: [Architect] — Define index and directory structure
items.description: Master index format (registry of all KBs, cross-topic mappings), per-KB index format (file listing by topic), per-KB manifest format (file status and sync history), cross-reference rules (results ranked by authority score), file naming conventions, exact directory tree.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: KB architecture specified
gate_conditions: KB complexity decision documented with rationale
If multi-layer: every knowledge type from Phase 1 research assigned to exactly one layer
If multi-layer: no two layers cover the same knowledge type (separation rule verified)
Entry schema defined with all required fields, no placeholders
Bridge schema defined if domain requires translation layer
If bridge not needed: explicit justification documented
Population pipeline defined with source, quality criteria, and curation rules
Index and cross-reference structure defined with exact file formats
Directory tree specified down to file naming convention
blocker_examples: Chose 'structured multi-layer' for a simple ops checklist that has one knowledge type — over-engineered, switch to flat
Two layers both claim 'implementation patterns' — overlapping boundaries, merge or redefine separation rules
Entry schema lists fields but no example entry — an agent can't verify the schema works without a concrete example, add one

excluded_files: scope.md and constraints.md — KB Bootstrapping does not need them; they re-enter context at Phase 4
research/requirements.md — needed at Phase 4, not Phase 3

guardrail_checks: KB complexity level matches complexity_profile.knowledge dimension from Phase 0 — if flat domain has bridged KB design, or bridged domain has flat KB, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 3: KB Bootstrapping
checklists.purpose: Execute the KB blueprint from Phase 2: create the directory tree, seed placeholder entries, and harvest initial content from research documents. The KB must exist and be populated before process architecture can reference it.

compilation.role_mindset: Builder — executing the KB blueprint with mechanical precision
compilation.objective: Create the KB directory tree, seed all placeholder entries, and harvest initial content from research documents
pre_check: entry-schema.json exists with all required fields defined
directory-structure.md exists with exact directory tree specified
population-strategy.md exists with harvesting sources identified
success_criteria: KB directory tree matches directory-structure.md exactly
One placeholder entry per topic per layer created and conforms to entry-schema.json
All harvestable research content captured in KB entries (zero skipped items)
Master-index.json and per-layer manifests reflect actual entry counts
If bridge layer: at least one bridge entry per descriptor category conforming to bridge-schema.json

items.title: [Builder] — Create KB directory tree
items.description:
Create the exact directory tree specified in directory-structure.md. Every directory in the tree must exist. Every _archive subdirectory must exist. Create master-index.json at the root. Create per-layer manifest.json files.

Verify: directory count matches directory-structure.md specification exactly.
items.output: kb/ directory tree, master-index.json, per-layer manifest.json files

items.title: [Builder] — Seed placeholder entries
items.description:
Create one placeholder entry per topic per layer as defined in population-strategy.md. Each placeholder must conform to entry-schema.json with status='placeholder' and contain: id, kb, topic, status, version (0.1.0), title, summary (one sentence describing what this entry will contain), empty description.

Verify: placeholder count matches the topic count from kb-architecture.md.
items.output: kb/ placeholder entries (one per topic per layer)

items.title: [Builder] — Harvest initial content from research documents
items.description:
Walk through research/domain-analysis.md, research/best-practices.md, and research/cross-cutting-concerns.md. For each knowledge item that maps to a KB layer topic, populate the corresponding placeholder entry with harvested content. Set status='harvested'.

If replacing an existing playbook and its KB data was flagged for harvest in Phase 1, include that source.

Update per-layer manifest.json and master-index.json with entry counts.

Verify: all harvestable items from research documents are captured. Zero placeholders remain for topics with available research data.

items.title: [Builder] — Create bridge entries
items.conditional: Only if bridge layer was defined in Phase 2
items.description:
Create bridge entries per bridge-schema.json for the most common translation mappings identified in research. Each bridge entry maps a subjective descriptor to parameter ranges with confidence scores.

Minimum: one bridge entry per identified descriptor category from research/domain-analysis.md.

Confidence score differentiation: do NOT assign the same confidence score to every bridge entry. Scores must reflect actual evidence strength: entries backed by multiple research sources or established conventions get higher scores (0.7-1.0); entries based on inference or single-source data get lower scores (0.3-0.6); speculative entries get lowest scores (0.1-0.2). If all entries have identical scores, the bridge layer provides no ranking signal.

Verify: bridge entries conform to bridge-schema.json, all required fields present, confidence scores between 0.0 and 1.0, and at least two distinct confidence values across all entries.

items.title: [Auditor] — Validate file paths and schema conformance
items.description:
Before the gate check, validate:

1. File-path audit: every file referenced in master-index.json and per-layer manifests exists on disk. Report any orphaned references or missing files.
2. Schema conformance: load entry-schema.json, then validate every KB entry against it. Check ALL required fields, types, and values — including entry ID format. If entry-schema.json defines an ID pattern (e.g., {kb}_{topic}_{entry-name}), every entry ID must match it. Do not accept ad-hoc ID formats that diverge from the schema.
3. If bridge layer exists: load bridge-schema.json and validate every bridge entry. Check confidence scores are numeric and in range [0.0, 1.0].
4. Artifact-manifest audit: verify artifact-manifest.md lists every file produced in this phase. Count files on disk and compare to manifest entry count. Report any untracked files.

Produce a validation-report.md listing: files checked, schema violations found (with entry ID and field), manifest gaps, and a PASS/FAIL summary. This report is evidence for the gate.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: KB bootstrapped and populated
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). Reference validation-report.md for schema conformance evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 4.
gate_conditions: KB directory tree exists and matches directory-structure.md specification
All placeholder entries created (one per topic per layer)
All harvestable research content has been captured in KB entries
Master-index.json and per-layer manifests reflect actual entry counts
If bridge layer: at least one bridge entry per descriptor category
Entry schema validation: every entry conforms to entry-schema.json
Validation report: all file paths resolve and all entries pass schema check
Artifact-manifest.md tracks every file produced in this phase — no untracked files
guardrail_checks: KB complexity level matches complexity_profile.knowledge dimension from Phase 0 — if flat domain has bridged KB design, or bridged domain has flat KB, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding
blocker_examples: Directory tree created but no placeholder entries — KB is empty shell, not bootstrapped
Research documents contain 20 harvestable items but only 5 were captured — incomplete harvest
Bridge entries created but with no confidence scores — doesn't conform to bridge-schema.json

next_phase_context: kb-architecture.md (summary — layer names and boundaries only)
excluded_files: Full KB entries — Process Architecture only needs layer names for phase-to-KB mapping
Population strategy — relevant during execution, not during process design
research/domain-analysis.md — knowledge types now captured in KB entries
research/best-practices.md — content now harvested into KB entries

checklists.title: Phase 4: Process Architecture
checklists.purpose: Design the output playbook's phase structure, task granularity, dependencies, and gates.

context_load: kb-architecture.md (summary — layer names and boundaries only)
compilation.role_mindset: Architect — structure, design, map. Fresh session benefits from reviewing with new eyes.
compilation.objective: Design the output playbook's complete phase structure with task granularity, dependencies, gates, and document tree
success_criteria: Phase structure covers full process from start to finish
Task granularity standard documented
Dependencies mapped with no circular dependencies
Every phase has a gate with verifiable conditions
Document tree complete

items.title: [Architect] — Define phase structure for the output playbook
items.description:
Phase design principles:
1. Each phase is a coherent block of work with a clear objective
2. A phase's output is the next phase's input
3. Every phase ends with a gate — explicit approval criteria before proceeding
4. Early phases: understanding (audit, research). Middle: doing (build, create). Late: verifying and operating (QA, launch, monitor)
5. Cross-cutting concerns woven into relevant phases, not isolated

items.title: [Architect] — Define task granularity standard
items.description:
A task represents ONE deliverable or ONE decision. If a task takes more than 4 hours or requires multiple skill sets, split it. If a task can't fail independently of the next task, merge them. Every task must be completable by the assigned role without ambiguity.

Title-only vs description rules:
- TITLE ONLY: simple, obvious actions
- SHORT DESCRIPTION: tasks with specific requirements
- DETAILED DESCRIPTION: tasks requiring methodology, syntax, decision criteria, or multi-step procedures

items.title: [Architect] — Map phase dependencies
items.description: For each phase: hard dependencies (must complete first), soft dependencies (should complete), parallel opportunities (can run simultaneously). Within phases: which tasks block others.

items.title: [Architect] — Design phase gates
items.description:
For each phase: what must be TRUE before the next phase starts, what deliverables must exist, what quality checks must pass.

Gate conditions must be VERIFIABLE, not subjective:
- Good: 'All 15 city pages have 300+ words of unique localized content'
- Bad: 'City pages are done'

Each gate includes blocker_examples — specific scenarios that would prevent advancement.

items.title: [Architect] — Identify early assessment/detection phases needed
items.description: Does this domain have variable starting conditions that affect the workflow? Does detection change the workflow? Does the playbook need an environment setup phase? Does it need a deconstruction/audit phase before implementation? If yes, design these as dedicated phases BEFORE any implementation work.

items.title: [Architect] — Define the deliverable document tree
items.description: Which tasks produce documents, file path/naming conventions, which documents feed into later tasks. Every task that says 'Document in X' must have X defined here.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review and approve architecture
items.description: Phase structure covers the full process. No gaps between phases. Phase gates are meaningful, not rubber stamps. Task granularity matches target user capability. Architecture satisfies all requirements from research/requirements.md.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Architecture approved
gate_conditions: Phase structure covers full process from start to finish
Task granularity standard documented and approved
Dependencies mapped with no circular dependencies
Every phase has a gate with verifiable conditions and blocker examples
Early assessment/detection phases included if domain requires them
Document tree complete — every referenced document has a defined path
Architecture satisfies requirements.md
blocker_examples: Phase structure missing detection phase for platform-specific playbook — add before implementation
Gates are vague ('research done') — make verifiable
Document tree has placeholder paths — resolve before Phase 4

excluded_files: Dependency map detail — used during architecture, referenced if questions arise during task engineering
Full requirements.md — architecture already satisfies it
Document tree — referenced during task engineering if needed

guardrail_checks: Phase count matches complexity_profile.process dimension from Phase 0 — simple: 5-8 phases, standard: 8-13, complex: 12-18 — if outside range, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 5: Role Engineering
checklists.purpose: Define the functional roles for the output playbook. Who does what, who approves what, how do roles hand off work.

compilation.role_mindset: Architect — designing roles as capabilities, not org chart positions
compilation.objective: Define all functional roles, handoff points, and escalation paths for the output playbook

items.title: [Architect] — Define all roles for the output playbook
items.description:
For each role: name (bracket syntax: [RoleName]), one-line responsibility description, skills/knowledge required, tools/access needed, decision authority.

Role design principles:
1. Every task must have exactly one owner
2. No role should appear fewer than 3 times — if it does, expand scope or merge
3. Roles map to capabilities, not people
4. Include coordination roles, QA roles, and decision roles

items.title: [Architect] — Define handoff points between roles
items.description: Where does one role's output become another role's input? For each handoff: what is transferred, in what format, what constitutes a complete handoff.

items.title: [Architect] — Define escalation paths
items.description: When a task is blocked, who resolves it? Technical blockers, business/strategy questions, quality disputes, resource conflicts, scope questions. For single-agent systems: escalation = ask the human.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Roles defined, handoffs documented
items.description: Note: orphaned/undefined role verification happens in Phase 8 (JSON Assembly) after tasks are written.
gate_conditions: All roles defined with responsibilities, required skills, and decision authority
Role count is appropriate for playbook complexity (minimum 2, justified if more than 6)
Handoff points documented for every role transition
Escalation paths defined
blocker_examples: Role appears in only one task — expand scope or merge with another role
Role mentioned in tasks but not defined — add definition
No escalation path for technical blockers — define before proceeding

next_phase_context: kb-architecture.md (layer names — needed for writing output playbook handoff blocks)
research/cross-cutting-concerns.md (needed for weaving concerns into tasks)
excluded_files: Role engineering discussion and alternatives considered — captured in role-definitions.md
Escalation paths and handoff points — referenced during task writing if needed

guardrail_checks: Role count matches complexity_profile.roles dimension from Phase 0 — minimal: 2-3 roles, standard: 3-5, full: 4-8 — if outside range, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 6: Task Engineering
checklists.purpose: Write every task in the output playbook. This is where most of the output quality is created.

compilation.role_mindset: Builder — writing concrete tasks, not designing structure. Every task must be executable by reading title + description alone.
compilation.objective: Write all task titles, descriptions, gates with handoff blocks, and weave cross-cutting concerns throughout
success_criteria: All tasks written with titles and descriptions per granularity standard
Implementation methods specified on all technical tasks
Every phase has a compilation block and gate task with handoff block
Cross-cutting concerns appear in 3+ phases each
No placeholder text anywhere

items.title: [Builder] — Write all task titles
items.description:
Title format: [Role] — Action verb + specific deliverable

Rules:
1. Start with [Role] bracket
2. Use action verbs: Build, Create, Configure, Audit, Validate, Document, Review, Deploy, Test, Fix
3. Be specific: 'Build homepage' not 'Work on homepage'
4. Include quantity or scope where relevant
5. Every title must be understandable without reading the description

Write all tasks in drafts/task-list-v0.1.md first. JSON comes later.

items.title: [Builder] — Write task descriptions for all non-obvious tasks
items.description:
WHEN to include: task has specific requirements, requires methodology, has acceptance criteria beyond 'done', involves a decision with criteria, has anti-patterns, produces a document, has dependencies.

DESCRIPTION STRUCTURE:
- WHAT: what exactly is being produced
- HOW: methodology, tools, commands, syntax rules
- SPECS: quantitative requirements
- DON'T: anti-patterns and common mistakes
- OUTPUT: document path or deliverable name
- VERIFY: how to confirm the task is done correctly

QUALITY CHECK: Could someone unfamiliar with this project execute this task using only the description?

items.title: [Builder] — Include implementation method on all technical tasks
items.description:
For every implementation task, specify: which tools/interfaces to use, where content/data lives, what scope the edit has, what syntax rules or constraints apply, what NOT to do, what to test after the edit.

A task that says 'build X' without specifying how is incomplete.

items.title: [Builder] — Include risk levels on tasks that affect shared resources
items.description: Any task that edits a global or shared element must include: SCOPE (isolated / template-level / global), BLAST RADIUS (what else is affected), RISK LEVEL (low / medium / high), ROLLBACK (how to undo), TEST AFTER (specific things to verify).

items.title: [Builder] — Write phase compilation blocks and gate tasks with handoff blocks
items.description:
Every phase opens with a compilation block: context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant.

context_load is derived from the previous phase's next_phase_context plus decisions-ledger.md and artifact-manifest.md.
pre_check conditions must be verifiable — typically the previous phase's gate conditions.
failure_modes_relevant is [] for v1.0 playbooks.

Optional compilation fields for agent tuning: success_criteria (what the phase must produce — mirrors gate_conditions so agent sees targets at phase start), tools_available (restricts agent to relevant capabilities), behavioral_profile (risk_tolerance, creativity_level, verbosity, stance).

Every phase ends with a gate task assigned to [Coordinator].
Gate format: '[Coordinator] — Phase gate: [comma-separated verifiable conditions]'
Every gate includes blocker_examples and handoff block: output_artifacts, next_phase_context, excluded_files, skill_validation.

items.title: [Builder] — Weave cross-cutting concerns into relevant tasks
items.description: From cross-cutting concerns identified in Phase 1. Each concern must appear in at least 3 phases. Cross-cutting concerns that only appear once are audit failures.

items.title: [Builder] — Create per-phase execution guides for critical phases
items.description:
For each phase marked critical in the process architecture, produce a standalone execution guide (phases/phase-N-name.md) containing: overview, purpose, pre-checks, task-by-task instructions with KB lookups where applicable, gate criteria, and common pitfalls.

Execution guides are more usable than raw JSON for human developers. Not every phase needs one — only phases with complex multi-step procedures or domain-specific judgment calls.

items.title: [Builder] — Create reusable templates for key deliverables
items.description:
For each phase that produces a structured document (specification, test plan, review checklist, audit report), create a blank template with the expected structure, headings, and placeholder prompts.

Templates lower the barrier for developers executing the playbook by showing exactly what a completed deliverable looks like.

items.title: [Auditor] — Review all tasks for completeness and clarity
items.description:
Binary verification checklist:
- Does each task have a [Role] owner? Y/N
- Is each title specific and actionable? Y/N
- Does each non-obvious task have a description? Y/N
- Does each description answer what, how, and how to verify? Y/N
- Do implementation tasks include method specification? Y/N
- Do shared-resource tasks include risk levels? Y/N
- Is there any placeholder text (TBD, TODO)? Y/N
- Is terminology consistent across all tasks? Y/N
- Do file paths in descriptions match the document tree? Y/N
- Does the [Role] in each title match the owner field? Y/N

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: All tasks engineered
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 7.

Risk levels assigned on shared-resource tasks

Every phase has a gate task with handoff block

Templates produced for phases with structured deliverables (templates/*.md)
[Auditor] review passed with no unresolved issues
No placeholder text anywhere

Cross-cutting concern only appears in the design phase — must also appear in build, QA, and monitoring phases
Gate handoff lists next_phase_context but no excluded_context — handoff is incomplete

Auditor review notes — issues resolved, fixes applied

checklists.title: Phase 7: Output Configuration
checklists.purpose: Define how the output playbook is used: workflow model, session strategy, KB mapping, skill activation, router, and post-run review guidance.

compilation.role_mindset: Architect — designing how the playbook operates, not what it contains
compilation.objective: Define workflow model, usage instructions, session strategy, KB mapping, skill activation, router, and post-run review
pre_check: All tasks engineered with titles and descriptions
cross-cutting concerns woven into 3+ phases each
success_criteria: Workflow model defined with justification
Usage instructions cover start, session breaks, and context carry
Phase-to-KB-layer mapping consistent with KB layer definitions
Compilation block tuning (success_criteria, tools_available, behavioral_profile) specified for output playbook phases
Router/dispatcher defined
Post-run review structure defined

items.title: [Architect] — Define workflow model and role descriptions
items.description: Workflow model: human-in-the-loop, fully autonomous, human-directed, or custom. Role descriptions for the output playbook (from Phase 4 role definitions, condensed for the JSON).

items.title: [Architect] — Define usage instructions
items.description: How to start: what context to provide for the first phase. Session strategy: which phases can share a session, where to break, what context to carry. Cost optimization: how to minimize token usage while maintaining quality. General operating rules that apply to all phases.

items.title: [Architect] — Define compilation block tuning for output playbook phases
items.description:
For each phase in the output playbook, specify optional compilation block fields that tune agent behavior:

- success_criteria (array of strings): What the agent must produce/achieve — surfaced at phase START so the agent works toward explicit targets. Should align with gate_conditions.
- tools_available (array of strings): Capability restriction — prevents role bleed by limiting what the agent can do (e.g., file_reading, file_creation, web_search, user_questioning, json_validation, script_execution).
- behavioral_profile (object): Phase-specific tuning with four dimensions: risk_tolerance (minimal|low|moderate|high), creativity_level (strict|conservative|moderate|exploratory), verbosity (minimal|concise|detailed|comprehensive), stance (supportive|neutral|critical|adversarial).

Guidelines: Research phases typically get moderate risk + exploratory creativity. Build/assembly phases get minimal risk + strict creativity. Audit phases get minimal risk + adversarial stance. All three fields are optional — omit them only for phases where generic behavior is acceptable.

items.title: [Architect] — Define phase-to-KB-layer mapping
items.description: For each phase in the output playbook: which KB layers are relevant. No phase loads the entire KB — only the layers it needs. Must be consistent with KB layer definitions from Phase 2.

items.title: [Architect] — Define skill activation mapping
items.description: For each phase: which prompting skill/mode to activate (or 'none'). Must be consistent with the skill field in each gate's handoff block. For new domains without existing skills, all values are 'none'. Skills are identified after execution runs and added in subsequent playbook versions.

items.title: [Architect] — Define router/dispatcher and context preservation specification
items.description:
Router: a short prompt or decision tree at the entry point. Given a user request, the router determines: which KB layers to load, which playbook phase applies, and which skill to activate.

For single-layer/flat KB playbooks: router is trivial.
For multi-layer KB playbooks: router maps request type to minimum KB slice.

Context preservation: define the two persistent files for the output playbook (decisions ledger and artifact manifest) — file paths, format, update rules, what never to exclude. File paths must match what compilation blocks reference in context_load.

items.title: [Architect] — Define post-run review structure
items.description: What to assess after the output playbook completes a run: what went well, what didn't, what should change, metrics target vs actual, quality assessment. This is guidance, not a template.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Output configuration complete
gate_conditions: Workflow model defined
Roles defined with responsibilities and decision authority
Usage instructions cover how to start, where to break sessions, what context to carry
Phase-to-KB-layer mapping is consistent with KB layer definitions from Phase 2
Skill activation is defined for every phase (even if 'none')
Router/dispatcher defined (or explicitly trivial for flat-KB playbooks)
Compilation block tuning defined for each phase (success_criteria, tools_available, behavioral_profile — omitted only where generic behavior is acceptable)

Skill activation inconsistent with gate handoff skill fields — fix one or the other

excluded_files: Session strategy rationale — captured in output-config.md
Alternative workflow models considered — final choice documented

checklists.title: Phase 8: Metrics & KPI Definition
checklists.purpose: Define measurable success criteria for the output playbook.

compilation.role_mindset: Researcher — defining what success looks like, not building it. Domain outcome metrics require understanding what the playbook is supposed to achieve.
compilation.objective: Define process, output quality, and domain outcome metrics with targets and measurement methods
pre_check: KB mapping and skill activation defined
success_criteria: At least one process metric defined with measurement method
At least one output quality metric defined with measurement method
At least one domain outcome metric defined with measurement method
All metrics have title, description, type, and target
Stakeholder approved metrics and targets

items.title: [Researcher] — Define process metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring the execution of the playbook itself: duration metrics (time to complete, time per phase), volume metrics (tasks completed, deliverables produced), quality metrics (issues found at QA, rework count, gate failures).

For each: title, description, type (metric_integer | metric_currency | metric_duration), category ('process'), target, measurement method.

items.title: [Researcher] — Define output quality metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring the QUALITY of the work produced: gate pass rate, audit findings count, description completeness, domain-specific quality measures.

For each: title, description, type, category ('output_quality'), target, measurement method.

items.title: [Researcher] — Define domain outcome metrics
items.description:
Metrics measuring whether the playbook achieved its PURPOSE. These are entirely domain-specific (downloads, revenue, coverage, compliance score, etc.). For optimization playbooks: include BEFORE and AFTER variants.

At least one metric in this category is mandatory — a playbook without outcome metrics can't prove it worked.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review and approve metrics
items.description: Metrics align with business goals from Phase 0. Targets are ambitious but achievable. Every metric has a clear measurement method. At least one metric in each of the three categories.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Metrics defined and approved
gate_conditions: At least one process metric defined
At least one output quality metric defined
At least one domain outcome metric defined
All metrics have title, description, type, and measurement method
Targets set where applicable
[Stakeholder] approved
blocker_examples: No domain outcome metric defined — a playbook that can't prove it worked is incomplete
Metric has no measurement method — define how to measure before proceeding

excluded_files: Metric alternatives discussed and rejected — final metrics captured
Task granularity and dependency docs — content reflected in the task list

guardrail_checks: Metrics count matches complexity_profile from Phase 0 — simple: 3-5 metrics, standard: 5-10, complex: 8-20 — if outside range, confirm with [Stakeholder] before proceeding

checklists.title: Phase 9: JSON Assembly
checklists.purpose: Assemble the complete output playbook JSON from all design documents. This phase focuses on assembly and syntax — structural validation happens in Phase 10.

compilation.role_mindset: Builder — assembling JSON from source documents. Mechanical precision, no creative interpretation.
compilation.objective: Assemble the complete output playbook JSON with all 16 required top-level fields and validate syntax
pre_check: At least one metric per category defined
success_criteria: JSON parses without errors
All 16 required top-level fields present
All checklists have title, purpose, compilation, and non-empty items array
Every item has title and owner fields

items.title: [Builder] — Assemble the playbook JSON structure
items.description:
MINIMUM EXECUTABLE PLAYBOOK STRUCTURE:

Required 16 top-level fields: title, version, description, workflow_model, roles, scope, cross_cutting_concerns, knowledge_base, checklists, metrics, usage_instructions, failure_modes, phase_kb_mapping, skill_activation, router, context_preservation.

Per-checklist (phase) required structure: title, purpose, compilation (object with context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant), items (non-empty array).

Per-item required fields: title (starts with [Role]), owner (matches [Role] in title). Optional: description, conditional, output.

Per-gate required fields: gate_conditions (array), blocker_examples (array), handoff (object with output_artifacts, next_phase_context, excluded_files).

Compilation block fields: context_load, role_mindset, objective, pre_check, failure_modes_relevant, agent_config, system_prompt_auto, context_budget, skill_preparation. Optional: success_criteria, tools_available, behavioral_profile.

A playbook with only phase names and gate conditions is a SUMMARY, not an executable playbook. Every phase must have a compilation block with context_load. Every non-obvious task must have a description with WHAT/HOW/VERIFY.

items.title: [Builder] — Validate JSON syntax
items.description:
Parse without errors. No trailing commas, unescaped characters, mismatched brackets. All string values properly escaped.

Verification: python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('drafts/playbook-v0.1.json'))"

items.title: [Auditor] — Validate assembled JSON structure and cross-references
items.description:
Before the gate check, validate the assembled playbook JSON:

1. Structural completeness: verify all 16 required top-level fields exist. For each checklist, verify title, purpose, compilation (with context_load), and non-empty items.
2. Cross-reference integrity: every file in a compilation.context_load must appear in a previous phase's handoff.output_artifacts. Every next_phase_context entry must map to an artifact the current phase produces.
3. Role consistency: every [Role] in item titles must match a role defined in the roles object.
4. Gate-criteria alignment: every success_criteria entry should map to at least one gate_condition.
5. Artifact-manifest audit: verify artifact-manifest.md tracks every file produced across all phases to date. Count files on disk and compare to manifest entry count. Report any untracked files.

Produce a structural-validation.md listing checks performed, violations found, and PASS/FAIL summary.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: JSON assembled and syntactically valid
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). Reference structural-validation.md for cross-reference evidence. A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 10.
gate_conditions: JSON parses without errors
All 16 required top-level fields present
All checklists have title, purpose, compilation, and non-empty items array
Every item has title and owner fields

Missing required top-level field — check the 16-field checklist

KB specification docs — embedded in JSON knowledge_base section

checklists.title: Phase 10: JSON Validation & Consistency
checklists.purpose: Validate the assembled JSON using automated validators and manual review. Fix all structural, role consistency, and schema errors before proceeding to quality audit.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — validating with fresh eyes. The JSON was assembled in a previous session; now verify it independently.

items.title: [Auditor] — Run automated validation and fix all errors
items.description:
Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py against the assembled JSON. If jsonschema is available, also run with --schema templates/output-schema.json. Fix all errors reported. Re-run until both validators pass with zero errors. Document any remaining warnings with explanations.

Covers: structural completeness, [Role] consistency, KB schema, compilation blocks, summary view consistency, failure_modes, metrics, CCC validation, handoff chain, and semantic checks.

items.title: [Auditor] — Manual review of assembled JSON
items.description: Read through entire playbook as a user would: Do tasks flow logically within each phase? Are descriptions consistent in tone and detail level? Would you know how to complete every task from title + description alone? Are metrics measurable with the tools/access defined?

checklists.title: Phase 11: Quality Audit — Gap Analysis
checklists.purpose: Systematic audit of the assembled playbook against requirements, cross-cutting concerns, phase flow, contradictions, completability, detail calibration, and KB integrity. Produces a prioritized fix list.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — reviewing with fresh eyes, not defending previous work. Binary yes/no judgments, no hedging.
compilation.objective: Audit the playbook across all quality dimensions and compile a prioritized fix list
success_criteria: Comprehensive audit completed covering all 7 dimensions with documented findings
Fix list compiled and prioritized (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
All phases, roles, and cross-cutting concerns covered by the audit

items.title: [Auditor] — Comprehensive quality audit
items.description:
Audit the playbook across all quality dimensions in a single pass. For each dimension, document findings as PASS/FAIL with specifics:

1. Requirements coverage: For each requirement in research/requirements.md, is it addressed by at least one task? Any requirements only partially addressed?
2. Cross-cutting concerns: For each concern, how many phases reference it? Any concerns appearing in fewer phases than minimum_phases?
3. Phase-to-phase flow: Does Phase N's output fully satisfy Phase N+1's inputs? Any gaps in the handoff chain?
4. Contradictions: Any tasks contradicting strategic constraints, other tasks, or the implementation method?
5. Task completability: Is every task assignable and completable given its role, inputs, and description?
6. Detail calibration: Any simple tasks over-described? Any complex tasks under-described?
7. KB buildability: Can an agent build the KB from the spec alone? Any contamination risk between layers?

items.title: [Auditor] — Compile audit findings into prioritized fix list
items.description: CRITICAL: contradictions, missing phases, broken dependencies. HIGH: cross-cutting gaps, incomplete descriptions, orphaned roles, unbuildable KB spec. MEDIUM: detail level issues, consistency problems. LOW: formatting, naming conventions, minor wording.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: All audits complete, fix list compiled

checklists.title: Phase 12: Stress Testing & Structured Dry-Run
checklists.purpose: Walk through the playbook under structured scenarios to find issues that gap analysis misses. Define a scenario matrix, execute walkthroughs from multiple perspectives, verify conditional logic and handoff chains, document friction, fix all issues, and get Auditor sign-off.

compilation.role_mindset: Auditor — adversarial thinking. Try to break the playbook by simulating real usage scenarios.
compilation.objective: Define scenario matrix, walk through the playbook under all scenarios, verify conditional logic and handoff chains, fix all issues
success_criteria: Scenario matrix defined with 2+ scenarios
All scenario walkthroughs completed
Handoff chain traced and verified
All CRITICAL, HIGH, and MEDIUM issues fixed
JSON re-validated after fixes
Auditor verification passed — no regressions

items.title: [Coordinator] — Define scenario matrix
items.description:
Define 2-3 scenarios with concrete parameters:

1. MINIMAL CASE: smallest possible project in this domain. Exercises the fewest tasks and conditional paths.
2. TYPICAL CASE: representative mid-complexity project. Exercises the most common path.
3. COMPLEX CASE (optional): high-complexity variant. Exercises conditional tasks, all KB layers, maximum role coverage.

For each scenario: name, brief description, which conditional tasks apply, expected KB complexity, expected number of phases exercised.

items.title: [Auditor] — Scenario walkthroughs
items.description:
For each scenario in the matrix, walk through every phase of the playbook:

Per-scenario checks:
- Can each task be completed given this scenario's parameters? Y/N
- What would the task produce for this scenario?
- Are there blockers, ambiguities, or missing information?
- Does the gate make sense for this scenario?

Scenario-specific perspectives to apply:
- Happy path: no problems — does it flow end to end?
- Domain novice: someone who has NEVER done this work — can they follow the tasks?
- KB construction: agent encountering domain for first time — can they build the KB from the spec?
- Blockers: what if access/tools are unavailable? What if QA fails?
- Domain variants: if the playbook covers variants, do all tasks make sense for each variant?

Document Y/N per task per scenario.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify conditional logic and trace handoff chain
items.description:
Conditional task logic: For each conditional task, does the condition evaluate correctly for each scenario? Are there ambiguous conditions? Missing conditional tasks?

Handoff chain trace: For each scenario, trace the full chain from Phase 0 to final phase. Does each phase's next_phase_context provide everything the next phase needs? Are there context_load items that no previous phase produces? Does the context budget allow loading all critical files at every phase?

items.title: [Auditor] — Edge cases and friction documentation
items.description:
Edge cases: minimal case (smallest project) — does it still work? Maximal case (largest, most complex) — does it scale? Legacy case (old technology/process) — does it accommodate? Partial case (project starts mid-stream).

Friction log: all questions that arose, ambiguities found, tasks needing more detail, tasks in wrong order, missing tasks.

Failure mode catalog: for every issue discovered, create FM entry (symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source).

items.title: [Builder] — Fix all issues from audit and stress testing
items.description: Resolve all issues in audits/fix-list.md, starting with CRITICAL, then HIGH, then MEDIUM. After each fix, verify no new contradictions introduced. For each fix: note what changed, verify the fix doesn't break anything else. Add new failure modes to failure_modes[] for issues discovered during testing.

items.title: [Builder] — Re-validate and produce tested JSON
items.description: Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py. Verify JSON parses, all roles consistent, compilation blocks intact, handoff chains unbroken. Save validated output as drafts/playbook-v0.2.json.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify all fixes and sign off
items.description:
Verify: all fixes are clean — no new contradictions, no regressions. JSON still validates. KB specification still buildable. Handoff chain still intact for all scenarios. Fix-list entries are resolved, not just closed.

If issues found: return to [Builder] for fixes, then re-verify. Do not advance.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Stress testing and dry-run complete
items.description: Produce a GATE VERIFICATION block: list each condition below with explicit PASS or FAIL and a one-line evidence citation (file path or content reference). A single FAIL blocks advancement to Phase 13.
gate_conditions: Scenario matrix defined with 2+ scenarios
All scenario walkthroughs completed with Y/N per task per scenario
Conditional task logic verified for all scenarios
Handoff chain traced and verified for all scenarios
Edge cases and friction documented
All CRITICAL, HIGH, and MEDIUM issues fixed
JSON re-validated after fixes
[Auditor] verification passed — no regressions
blocker_examples: Scenario walkthrough reveals unresolvable ambiguity in a task
Handoff chain broken — phase N+1 needs file that phase N doesn't produce
CRITICAL issue found that requires architectural change (escalate to Stakeholder)

excluded_files: Scenario walkthrough details — issues extracted and fixed
Pre-fix JSON draft — superseded by v0.2

checklists.title: Phase 13: Stakeholder Review & Iteration
checklists.purpose: Final human review before pilot testing.

compilation.role_mindset: Stakeholder — business alignment, strategic review. Does this playbook achieve what was commissioned?
compilation.objective: Human review of playbook against business strategy, roles, and success criteria. Specific feedback, then final approval.
success_criteria: Playbook reviewed against business strategy and success criteria from Phase 0
Roles and ownership reviewed — no overloaded roles, decision authority correctly placed
All stakeholder feedback is specific and actionable
Builder implemented all feedback changes
JSON re-validated after changes
Auditor verified no regressions from changes

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review playbook against business strategy
items.description: Does the playbook produce the right outcome? Are strategic constraints respected throughout? Are metrics aligned with business KPIs? Is the playbook parameterized properly (per-run variables, not hardcoded)? Would you trust this playbook to run without supervising every step?

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Review roles and ownership
items.description: Roles match available capabilities. No role is overloaded. Decision authority is correctly placed. Coordination role has enough visibility.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Provide feedback and change requests
items.description:
Specific, actionable feedback: tasks to add, remove, or modify; description changes needed; phase structure changes; metric or target adjustments.

'Make it better' is not feedback. Specific changes only.

items.title: [Builder] — Implement stakeholder feedback
items.description: Edit drafts/playbook-v0.2.json per stakeholder-feedback.md. Apply each change, verify compilation blocks and handoff chains remain consistent.

items.title: [Builder] — Re-validate JSON after changes
items.description: Run validate_playbook.py and validate_semantic.py. Save validated output as final/playbook-v1.0.json.

items.title: [Auditor] — Verify stakeholder changes don't introduce regressions
items.description: Spot-check that feedback implementation is clean — no new contradictions, no broken handoffs. Verify compilation blocks still consistent after any phase structure changes. If issues found: return to [Builder], then re-verify.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Final approval of playbook
items.description: Satisfies success criteria from Phase 0. All feedback addressed. Business strategy respected throughout. Would you run this playbook tomorrow with confidence?

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Stakeholder approved, Auditor verified
gate_conditions: All stakeholder feedback addressed
[Auditor] verification passed — no regressions from changes
Roles and ownership reviewed — no overloaded roles, decision authority clear
Final approval given
JSON valid after changes
Success criteria from Phase 0 are satisfied
blocker_examples: Stakeholder says 'looks fine' without reviewing specific phases — not approval, need documented review
Feedback says 'add more detail to Phase 3' without specifying which tasks — not actionable, request specifics

excluded_files: All feedback discussion — changes applied to JSON
Previous draft versions — superseded

checklists.title: Phase 14: Documentation & Version Control
checklists.purpose: Package the final playbook with supporting documentation.

compilation.role_mindset: Coordinator — packaging and archiving. Completeness and clarity for future users.
compilation.objective: Create changelog, archive research/audit docs, store production JSON, write quick-start guide
success_criteria: Changelog written with all version history entries
Research and audit documents archived
Production JSON stored in designated location with backup
Quick-start guide covers prerequisites, how to start, roles, and phase overview

items.title: [Coordinator] — Create playbook changelog
items.description: Version history with dates and change summaries: v0.1 (initial draft), v0.2 (post-audit fixes), v0.3 (post-stakeholder feedback), v1.0 (post-pilot, production ready).

items.title: [Coordinator] — Archive all research and audit documents
items.description: Preserve: research/, architecture/, audits/, testing/. These are the 'why' behind design decisions.

items.title: [Builder] — Store production playbook JSON
items.description: Final JSON in designated location. Naming: {playbook-name}-playbook.json. Never overwrite without backup of previous version.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Create quick-start guide
items.description: One-page guide: what this playbook is for, prerequisites before starting, how to start a run, key roles, phase overview (one line per phase), where to find documentation.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Compile final metrics report
items.description:
Read metrics-tracker.md. For each metric: compare final value against target from the metrics[] array. Produce a summary table:

| Metric | Target | Actual | Status |

Status: PASS (met target), MISS (below target), N/A (no target defined).

Include brief analysis: which metrics indicate process health, which indicate output quality, what to improve in the next run.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Documentation complete
gate_conditions: Changelog written
Research and audit docs archived
JSON in version control
Quick-start guide covers prerequisites, how to start, key roles, and phase overview
Final metrics report compiled with target vs actual comparisons
blocker_examples: Changelog missing version history — document all versions
Quick-start guide missing prerequisites — add before finalizing

excluded_files: All creation process artifacts — archived for reference, not needed for ongoing use

checklists.title: Phase 15: Continuous Improvement
checklists.purpose: After each completed run of the output playbook, review and optionally improve it. Manual and human-initiated — no automatic feedback loops.

compilation.role_mindset: Stakeholder — reviewing execution data, deciding what to change
compilation.objective: After each playbook run, collect review data, catalog failure modes, decide whether to update the playbook
pre_check: At least one run of the output playbook has been completed

items.title: [Coordinator] — After each playbook run: collect review data
items.description: Review the post-run assessment (using the post_run_review structure from Output Configuration). Compare actual metrics to targets. Note tasks consistently skipped, reordered, or added ad-hoc. Note where the KB spec was insufficient during construction.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Catalog failure modes from this run
items.description:
For every bug, crash, unexpected behavior, or degraded result encountered during the run: create a failure mode entry (id: FM-NNN sequential, symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention, phase, severity, source).

severity: crash (process cannot continue), error (wrong output), degraded (works but quality reduced), cosmetic (visual/formatting).
prevention: write as a concrete checklist item or gate condition.
phase: assign to the output playbook phase where this should be prevented or detected.

Add entries to failure_modes[] array. Update relevant phase compilation blocks with new FM-IDs.

items.title: [Stakeholder] — Decide whether to update the playbook
items.description: Review collected data and new failure modes. Decide: update now, update later, or no changes needed. If updating: specify what changes to make and why. This is a human decision — the agent does not auto-modify the playbook.

items.title: [Builder] — Implement playbook updates
items.description: Follow same quality standards: validate JSON, check structural completeness, verify no introduced contradictions. Integrate failure mode prevention items into relevant phase tasks or gate conditions. Update changelog.

items.title: [Coordinator] — Phase gate: Improvement cycle complete
items.description: Validate that the improvement cycle has been executed: run data collected, failure modes cataloged, and any approved updates implemented and re-validated.
gate_conditions: Run review data collected and documented
New failure modes cataloged with FM-IDs (or 'none found' documented)
Stakeholder decision on updates is recorded in decisions-ledger.md
If updates approved: changes implemented and JSON re-validated
blocker_examples: Run data says 'no issues' but pilot-friction.md from Phase 12 listed unresolved items — review data is incomplete
New failure modes described in prose but not formatted with FM-ID, severity, and prevention fields

excluded_files: Improvement cycle details — captured in decisions-ledger.md
